title: DbContext: The Heart of EF Core

scenes.say: Why is the DbContext at the heart of Entity Framework Core? What makes it so important for your code?

scenes.label: Unit
scenes.sub: DbContext tracks all changes as a single unit.
scenes.say: DbContext implements the unit of work pattern. It tracks every change you make to your entities as a single unit.
Here’s the flow: create a DbContext per request, track changes as you go, then save everything in one transaction.
DbContext tracks entities by default, so it knows what to update. But for read-only queries, use AsNoTracking for better performance.

scenes.question: Should you reuse DbContext across requests?
scenes.right: No! It causes memory leaks and stale data.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Should you reuse a DbContext across requests? No way. That leads to memory leaks and stale data headaches.
